ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Arthur Ashe — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Six-month HIV and coronary disease review with depression screening

text.paragraph: Six-month HIV and coronary disease review with depression screening. [S]

Mr. Ashe returns six months after his first visit. He has missed no doses. He has had no headache, weakness, rash, fever, or chest pain, and has not needed nitroglycerin. He is back to full-time writing and coaching. He gave a urine sample with this morning's blood tests. He answered the PHQ-9 with a score of 2 and has no thoughts of self-harm. He says that knowing his viral load is undetectable has eased his mind. [S]

tr.td: Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema

Continue the same regimen.
Viral load, CD4 count, blood count, and metabolic panel at nine months.
Urine albumin yearly.

Cerebral toxoplasmosis on maintenance therapy (B58.2). No symptoms; CD4 above 200 for three months. [S]
Continue trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; if the CD4 count is still above 200 at nine months, stop it.

Coronary artery disease after two bypass operations (I25.10). No angina; blood pressure at goal; LDL 52 mg/dL three months ago. PHQ-9 2. [S]
Continue aspirin, atorvastatin, and ezetimibe.
